Extended Essay

An essential component of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme is the Extended Essay (EE). It is a research paper that gives pupils the chance to look into a subject of personal interest, typically one of the IB program’s disciplines. Students can conduct in-depth study for the Extended Essay and improve their writing, research, and critical thinking abilities.

Here are some key features and aspects of the Extended Essay:

  • Length: The essay’s normal word count is between 3,000 and 4,000, however there is no set number.
  • Subject Selection: The list of eligible IB courses or interdisciplinary themes is used by students to select a topic for their Extended Essay.
  • Research Question: For the Extended Essay, students must develop a clear research question that will guide their writing. This inquiry ought to be precise, understandable, and conducive to a thorough investigation.
  • Independent Research: Students are expected to do independent research to compile pertinent facts, figures, and proof to back up their claims or analyses.
  • Supervisor: Each student has a supervisor who mentors and supports them throughout the research and writing process. This supervisor is typically a teacher from the student’s school.
  • Assessment: Examiners for the International Baccalaureate (IB) grade the Extended Essay externally using a set of evaluation criteria. The essay counts towards the final grade for the IB Diploma.
  • Formal Requirements: An essay’s structure, formatting, and bibliography should all be appropriate. Citations and a bibliography should be included to acknowledge the sources utilised in the study.

    • The Extended Essay gives students the chance to delve deeply into a subject they are passionate about, to show off their academic prowess, and to practise the kind of research and writing that will be required of them in further education. It encourages independent study and research, assisting students in acquiring crucial abilities for their future academic and professional endeavours.
    The extended essay is a fantastic chance for students to research a subject they are interested in and gain crucial skills that will be useful in both their academic and future professional endeavours. It takes a lot of time, work, and attention, but for students who approach it with interest and enthusiasm, it can also be a rewarding experience.
